Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with lower abdominal pain and feeling hot and sweaty for two days.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Having some, some pain, uh, in my tummy, like the lower part of my tummy. Um and I've just been feeling, quite, hot and sweaty... About two days ago.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The pain is located below the belly button (suprapubic), described as a gradual onset, constant, progressively worsening burning pain.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: like below my belly button... it's more gradual and it's just, it is getting a bit worse now... it's kind of like a, a, I guess a burning pain... It's pretty constant

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports urinary frequency (peeing more regularly) and noticed pink-colored urine, but denies dysuria (burning or stinging on urination).
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I did notice I was going to the, I was peeing more, regularly... the urine was a little pink, in colour. But I haven't like, it hasn't really been burning, specifically or hurting when I pee

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient had constipation last week, but bowel movements are now normal.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I had a bit of constipation, but that's better, now. That was like, since last week... my bowel movements are normal now.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient feels slightly nauseous but has not vomited.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Just a little nauseous, um, but no vomiting.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has felt hot and sweaty but has not measured a temperature.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I felt a bit hot and sweaty, but I haven't really measured it, so I can't really say.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or vision problems.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I don't feel short of breath... I don't have a cough... Any uh, funny heartbeats or rhythms, palpitations? Not that it, no... Any headaches? Any problems with your vision? No.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has no past medical or surgical history.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: I haven't had any, surgical, I don't have any surgical history... I don't have any previous, I haven't had any operations before

Medications.content: Patient's only medication is the Implanon contraceptive implant, inserted one year ago.
Medications.source_text: I'm, on the Implanon. I had the Implanon inserted about a year ago.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is sexually active with the same partner. Last sexual contact was four days ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I have had the same partner, I am, we were last sexually active about four days ago.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Last STD screen was normal six months ago. Uses Implanon for contraception with no other barrier method.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: my last STD screen was normal, which was about six months ago... we don't use any other barrier, method so, we just use the , I just have the Implanon

Social_and_Family_History.content: Last menstrual period was two weeks ago.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Uh, my last period was about, three weeks ago. I mean, two weeks ago.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient lives in a shared house with two roommates and works as an accountant.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I live in a share house, and with two other, two other room-mates... I am an accountant.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Do you smoke at all, Kim? No... socially I drink

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has no relevant family history.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Any other family history I should be aware of? No, not that , not that I'm aware of, no.

Assessment.content: The differential diagnosis includes a urinary tract infection (UTI), a gut-related issue, or a pregnancy-related cause.
Assessment.source_text: Could just be a, you know, could just be a urine infection, for example. Could just be something related to your gut... could just be something related to your, you know, a pregnancy-related cause.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to take a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: maybe worth taking a pregnancy test later on, just to confirm that.

Plan_of_Care.content: Perform urine tests (urine dip and MSU).
Empirically treat for a UTI with antibiotics: Trimethoprim, one tablet twice a day for three days.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: it's probably maybe worth empirically treating you for a maybe urine infection... start the antibiotics today, something called Trimethoprim. Um, you can take two tablets, uh, one tablet twice a day for three days.

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommended regular Paracetamol for pain, increased fluid intake, and trying cranberry juice.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: you can try just regular painkillers, uh, Paracetamol would be advisable. Um, make sure you drink plenty of fluids. You can try some cranberry juice as well

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review in a few days (or 24-48 hours) if symptoms are not improving or are worsening.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: And, um, and I want you to kind of really come back and see me in a few days time, if your symptoms are not getting any better, or indeed if they're getting worse.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised on red flag symptoms for urgent review: worsening abdominal pain, persistent fever/sweats, or vomiting.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: So, things to look out for would be, you know, worsening tummy pain, um, if you're feeling really hot or sweaty, your temperature's not coming down um, vomiting et cetera.
